decisions.statement: A stylesheet's rules are a page property held in a file beside the page.
A stylesheet is its own page rather than a property of the components the stylesheet dresses.
One stylesheet dresses as many components as name the stylesheet's classes.
A component is dressed by naming a class rather than by importing a stylesheet.
A component imports a stylesheet only to make a bundler emit the stylesheet.
A stylesheet page names the components its rules dress.
A stylesheet is formatted and linted by the run that reads a body of code.
A stylesheet is held to the same byte ceiling as any other file.
A stylesheet declares nothing a compiler could type.
A comment in a stylesheet is refused as prose in code is.
A specifier naming a stylesheet that is not there is refused by the typechecker.

definition: the rules a browser dresses something by
